title: Types of Farming Systems in India
subject: Geography
topic: Types of Farming in India – Overview
description: A classification diagram outlining the four principal farming systems in India: Rain-fed, Irrigated, Hilly & Terrace, and Coastal & Saline-affected, detailing their geographical extent, key crops, rainfall, and soil characteristics.
mermaidCode: graph TD A[Types of Farming in India] --> B(Rain-fed / Barani) B --> B1[~55% Cultivated Area] B --> B2[Crops: Millet, Sorghum, Pulses, Oilseeds] B --> B3[Rainfall: 300-800mm] B --> B4[Soil: Alluvial to Loamy, Low Water-holding] A --> C(Irrigated / Khadar-based) C --> C1[~45% Cultivated Area] C --> C2[Crops: Wheat, Rice, Sugarcane, Maize] C --> C3[Rainfall: >800mm] C --> C4[Soil: Fertile Alluvial, High Organic Matter] A --> D(Hilly & Terrace Farming) D --> D1[~7% Total Area] D --> D2[Crops: Maize, Potatoes, Tea, Horticulture] D --> D3[Rainfall: 800-1500mm] D --> D4[Soil: Lateritic, Shallow, Prone to Erosion] A --> E(Coastal & Saline-affected Farming) E --> E1[~3% Area] E --> E2[Crops: Coconut, Cashew, Shrimp Aquaculture] E --> E3[Rainfall: >1000mm (Monsoonal)] E --> E4[Soil: Sandy Loam, High Salinity, Water-logging]
